title: Christie Modlin:
title_q: “You Don’t Hear About It on the News”
title_short: Christie Modlin · You Don’t Hear About It on the News
headline: A tribal leader and NIWRC board member says the quiet part about the missing and murdered: when Native people go missing, it is not on the news. Then she shows what her tribe built instead, and why she serves.
story: Christie Modlin is Secretary of the Iowa Tribe of Oklahoma and sits on the NIWRC board. The reception was in a building owned by her tribe’s chairman, Jacob Keyes. Asked what she would change, she went straight to the MMIP crisis and local law enforcement. Asked what makes her hopeful, she named NIWRC. Asked for one message for the world, she said all of us are precious.

This is a hard-truth hook with a hopeful spine: the news does not cover it, so her tribe built a safe house, and NIWRC takes it to the Hill. Stay on her face. No MMIW imagery of any kind, no red handprint, no red dress, no stock. The words carry it.

Loops: L1 “Who goes missing and why don’t we hear?” opens at 0:00 and closes at 0:05 (“our women and our children”). L2 “So what is anyone doing about it?” opens at 0:00 and closes in the TURN (“a safe house for our women”) and the BUTTON (“all of us are precious”). Stakes: Native people go missing and it does not make the news.
